theme: Spatial Orientation, Map Scale & Grid Coordinate Systems

conceptual_foundation.introduction: Teaches spatial awareness and route navigation through crane migration paths, city maps, school floor plans, metro rail networks, and grid coordinates.

core_concepts.explanation: Orienting maps using the four main cardinal directions: North (top), South (bottom), East (right), and West (left).
core_concepts.example: On standard maps, North points toward the top of the page.

core_concepts.explanation: A map scale defines the fixed ratio between a unit distance on the map layout and the actual physical distance on the ground.
core_concepts.example: If Map Scale is '1 cm = 5 km', then a measured map route of 4 cm represents 4 × 5 = 20 km on the ground.

core_concepts.explanation: Interpreting symbols, color codes, and line paths on transportation maps (e.g. Delhi Metro network lines) to find transfer stations and optimal travel routes.
core_concepts.example: Blue line intersecting Yellow line indicates an interchange station.

core_concepts.explanation: Locating exact positions on a 2D grid map using ordered coordinate pairs (x, y). Moving horizontally along the x-axis first (column), then vertically along the y-axis (row).
core_concepts.example: Position (3, 4) means column 3 East, row 4 North.

core_concepts.explanation: Measuring movement along grid lines (east-west and north-south steps) to determine shortest navigation paths.
core_concepts.example: Moving from (1, 1) to (4, 5) requires (4 - 1) = 3 horizontal steps and (5 - 1) = 4 vertical steps = 7 total grid steps.

key_formulas_and_rules: Actual Distance = Map Measured Distance × Scale Factor
Coordinate Format: (x-column, y-row) - Always read horizontal X first!
Taxicab Grid Distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) = |x2 - x1| + |y2 - y1|
real_world_applications: GPS navigation apps, city urban planning, architectural floorplan blueprints, treasure hunt games, and logistics fleet routing.
